para.verbatim:
embed:rst The hashes related to the mod and its fix :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A :cpp:class:`ModType` constructed without one gets a **fully-populated** :cpp:class:`Hashes` (every hash the software ships with), not an empty table :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: A ``shared_ptr`` rather than a by-value member, for the same two reasons as #iniParseBuilder: :cpp:class:`ModType` must stay cheap to copy (it is returned by value from :cpp:func:`ModTypeIdTools::getModType` and stored by value in :cpp:member:`IniFile::modTypes`), and copying one must *share* its hashes rather than clone them .. note:: :cpp:class:`Hashes` is mutable (:cpp:func:`ModMappedAssets::addRepoRows`/ :cpp:func:`ModMappedAssets::addMap`), so two :cpp:class:`ModType`\\s deliberately handed the *same* ``shared_ptr`` share those mutations. Each one built with the ``nullptr`` default instead gets its own table

embed:rst The indices related to the mod and its fix :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Same default as #hashes: a :cpp:class:`ModType` constructed without one gets a **fully-populated** :cpp:class:`Indices` (every index the software ships with), not an empty table :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: A ``shared_ptr``, per-:cpp:class:`ModType` by default and shared on copy, for exactly the reasons spelled out on #hashes -- see that member's two notes

embed:rst The vertex counts related to the mod :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A :cpp:class:`ModType` constructed without one gets a **fully-populated** :cpp:class:`VertexCounts`, not an empty table :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: Unlike #hashes and #indices this is a :cpp:class:`ModDictAssets` rather than a :cpp:class:`ModMappedAssets`, so it has no ``getMap``/``hasFrom`` -- see :cpp:class:`VertexCounts` for why. Ownership works identically though: a ``shared_ptr``, per-:cpp:class:`ModType` by default and shared on copy

embed:rst The vertex group remaps for the mod -- maps the blend indices of this mod's vertex groups onto another mod's :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. warning:: **Its default differs from the other three asset tables.** #hashes, #indices and #vertexCounts each get a *fresh* table when not supplied; this one falls back to the single **shared** :cpp:func:`ModDataAssets::vgRemaps`. So mutating a defaulted ``vgRemaps`` affects every other :cpp:class:`ModType` that also defaulted, whereas mutating a defaulted ``hashes`` does not. That asymmetry is deliberate -- this is much the largest of the tables .. note:: Otherwise the ownership rules are the same as #hashes: a ``shared_ptr``, shared on copy

embed:rst The ``match_index_count`` of each of the mod's draw slots (WuWa) :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The first of the four WWMI-only asset tables, each an :cpp:class:`Indices` sibling keyed ``(version, name, component, type)`` with the draw slot as ``type``: this one, #vgOffsets, #vgCounts and #shapeKeyChecksums. They default the way #hashes does -- a fresh, fully-populated table with an empty remap map, which for a GI mod type holds no row of its own and remaps onto nothing

briefdescription.para: The vg_offset of each of the mod's draw slots (WuWa) see indexCounts.
The vg_count of each of the mod's draw slots (WuWa) see indexCounts.
The shape-key checksum of the mod (WuWa) see indexCounts.

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The draw passes of each of the mod's draw slots (WuWa) -- see :cpp:class:`DrawPasses` and #getDrawPass :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The first of six versioned tables of a character's GAME data that a fix reads at the run's version rather than carrying it: this, #textureRegisters, #gameShaders, #shapeKeyDispatchSizes, #boneCentroids and #shapeKeyRemaps. They default as #hashes does: a fresh, fully-populated table each

briefdescription.para: Where the mod's own draws bind each texture role see :cpp:class:TextureRegisters and getTextureRegister.
The game pixel shaders a fix draws the mod's parts with see :cpp:class:GameShaders and getGameShader.
The height WWMI dispatches the mod's shape keys with see :cpp:class:ShapeKeyDispatchSizes.
Each bone's rest-pose centroid on the mod's own model see :cpp:class:BoneCentroids and getBoneCentroids.
The order the mod's shape keys are put in on another character see :cpp:class:ShapeKeyRemaps and getShapeKeyRemap.
What the codes of the mod's single-channel code maps mean see :cpp:class:MaterialCodes and getMaterialCode.
The colours the mod's material masks mark each material with see :cpp:class:MaterialColours and getMaterialColour.
How the game creates the mod's game textures see :cpp:class:TextureDescs and getTextureDesc.
What the mod's game textures look like, as thumbprints see :cpp:class:TextureThumbprints and getTextureThumbprints.

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The builder that builds the parser for a ``.ini`` file of this type of mod :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A *factory*, not a parser: :cpp:func:`IniFile::parse` builds a **fresh** parser per ``.ini`` file from it, passing that file's :cpp:member:`IniFile::version` along, so a mod type can use a different parser for a 4.0-era ``.ini`` file than for a 5.7-era one -- see :cpp:class:`IniParseBuilder` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: The built parser arrives already bound to its own file, so two :cpp:class:`IniFile`\\s of the same mod type never share a parser's binding .. note:: A ``shared_ptr`` rather than a ``unique_ptr`` because :cpp:class:`ModType` must stay **copyable** -- :cpp:func:`ModTypeIdTools::getModType` returns one by value, and :cpp:member:`IniFile::modTypes` stores them by value. It also lets every :cpp:class:`ModType` of a game share one builder

embed:rst The builder that builds the fixer for a ``.ini`` file of this type of mod :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A *factory*, not a fixer: :cpp:func:`IniFile::fix` builds a **fresh** fixer per ``.ini`` file from it, passing that file's :cpp:member:`IniFile::version` along, so a mod type can use a different fixer for a 4.0-era ``.ini`` file than for a 5.7-era one -- see :cpp:class:`IniFixBuilder` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: The built fixer arrives already bound to that file's own built parser, so nothing rebinds it afterwards and two :cpp:class:`IniFile`\\s of the same mod type never share a fixer -- as with #iniParseBuilder on the parser side .. note:: A ``shared_ptr`` for the same reasons as #iniParseBuilder -- :cpp:class:`ModType` must stay copyable, and every :cpp:class:`ModType` of a game shares one builder

embed:rst The builder that hands out the remover for a ``.ini`` file of this type of mod :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A *factory*: :cpp:func:`IniFile::removeFix` asks it for a remover per ``.ini`` file, and it hands one back already bound to that file :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: This behaves like #iniParseBuilder and #iniFixBuilder -- a fresh remover per :cpp:func:`IniRemoveBuilder::build`, bound to the caller's file and nobody else's .. note:: A ``shared_ptr`` for the same reasons as #iniParseBuilder: several :cpp:class:`ModType`\\s share one builder (notably every one falling back to :cpp:func:`GlobalIniRemoveBuilders::removeBuilder`), and a builder is immutable once constructed, so sharing it is free
